findings.failure_scenario: Crew(planning=True) with Task(description='Validate that 100% of records are processed') evaluates the f-string first, then %-formatting parses '100% of the work' as a '% o' (octal) spec that consumes the tools-string argument and raises TypeError (%o format: a number is required, not str); a trailing '%' raises ValueError (incomplete format); '%s' in the data raises TypeError (not enough arguments for format string). The exception propagates through _handle_crew_planning (crew.py:617, no try/except) and aborts kickoff() before any task runs.
findings.summary: Mixing an f-string with %-formatting makes the % operator re-interpret '%' characters from interpolated task data, so any '%' in a task description, expected output, agent role/goal, or tool description raises an exception in _create_tasks_summary.

findings.failure_scenario: Agent(knowledge_sources=[StringKnowledgeSource(content='Critical doc A'), StringKnowledgeSource(content='Critical doc B')]) with planning enabled -> _create_tasks_summary embeds only 'Critical doc A'; the planner LLM never sees 'Critical doc B' and produces a plan missing the constraints it contains. _get_agent_knowledge's own docstring promises a list of all sources, but the caller uses only element 0.
findings.summary: Only the first knowledge source is embedded in the plan summary (knowledge_list[0]), so every other knowledge source attached to the agent is silently dropped from the planning prompt.

findings.failure_scenario: Agent(knowledge_sources=[PDFKnowledgeSource(file_paths=['spec.pdf'])]) -> knowledge_list[0] is {PosixPath('knowledge/spec.pdf'): '<entire PDF text>'}; the planner prompt receives a Python dict repr with embedded quotes instead of usable knowledge text, and the full file contents are dumped unescaped into the prompt (also bloat for large files).
findings.summary: _get_agent_knowledge returns source.content verbatim, but content is only a str for StringKnowledgeSource; file-based sources (PDF/CSV/JSON/text/excel) store content as Dict[Path, str] and CrewDoclingSource as List[DoclingDocument], so the summary interpolates raw object reprs instead of knowledge text.

findings.failure_scenario: A knowledge source whose content evaluates to None yields knowledge_list == [None]; str([None]) == "[None]" passes the guard and the summary embeds "agent_knowledge": "[\"None\"]" — the check excludes nothing it was evidently meant to exclude, so the intended protection against null/non-string content never fires.
findings.summary: The guard 'str(knowledge_list) != "None"' is dead code: str() of a list is never the literal string "None" (it is "[...]" or "[None]"), so None or non-string content is still embedded.

findings.failure_scenario: StringKnowledgeSource(content='He said "hello"') -> the summary line becomes "agent_knowledge": "[\"He said "hello"\"]", producing malformed quoting the planning LLM can misparse; a trailing backslash in content escapes the closing quote and glues the next task's text into the value. Multi-line content (as in the new test fixture) also splits the value across lines.
findings.summary: Knowledge content is embedded into a quoted pseudo-JSON value without escaping, so double quotes, backslashes, or newlines in the content break the quoting and structure of the planner prompt.

findings.failure_scenario: Dead import introduced by the change: the file uses no json module call, so linters (e.g. ruff F401 in CI) flag it and it suggests a planned-but-missing serialization step for the summary generation.
findings.summary: The added 'import json' is never used anywhere in planning_handler.py.

findings.failure_scenario: Grep shows Optional, MagicMock, and BaseModel appear only on the import lines (1, 2, 5); they are dead imports that static checkers in CI fail on and that mislead readers about what the tests exercise.
findings.summary: The diff adds 'from typing import Optional', 'MagicMock', and 'from pydantic import BaseModel' to the test module, none of which are used anywhere in the file.

findings.failure_scenario: Dead test fixture introduced by the change; its content is discarded and never exercised, so the multi-line/unescaped-newline path through the agent_knowledge formatting (a real weakness of the new summary code) goes untested while appearing covered.
findings.summary: The mock_knowledge_source fixture (lines 16-30) is never requested by any test in the module — the only test builds its own StringKnowledgeSource inline.
